statement: The raw all-type path categories form a strictly unital associative Cat-enrichment; their nerves and product-preserving Kan replacements give a simplicial category and a Segal model.
notes: No mapping-space comparison is required for the raw enrichment.

statement: Weak-vertical hammocks give a composition-compatible model of simplicial localization; this theorem alone does not replace arbitrary vertical arrows.
notes: Dwyer–Kan Definition 2.1 and Propositions 3.1, 3.3; exact all-type comparison in B.2.

statement: Pointed Cartesian composition cannot give the intended zero-preserving units unless identities equal zero; smash composition has the correct unit S0.
notes: The correction at IX ms.17 is verified with its exact unit.

statement: Cofibrant-fibrant objects in a pointed simplicial model category supply Kan mapping spaces with strict absorbing zero, smash composition, and S0-units.
notes: A sufficient modern setting; transfer to literal pointed stabilized paths is not silently inferred.

statement: Quillen’s fundamental groupoid agrees naturally with that of the derived mapping complex under cofibrant/fibrant replacement; specified vertices and basepoint paths determine the corresponding pi1 comparisons.
notes: For the literal full path category the comparison retains B.8 and pointed compatibility.

statement: Pointed infinity categories with the required pullbacks and pushouts have mapping-space loop/suspension formulas; a pointed derivator has the corresponding adjunction and exact morphisms.
notes: The hypotheses include enhanced homotopy limits and colimits; mere pi1-representability is insufficient.

statement: Representability of all pi1 mapping functors does not imply the mapping-space loop formulas.
notes: Full pointed infinity subcategory on *, S0 and K(Z,2); zero functors represent pi1 while the K(Z,1) loop space is noncontractible.

statement: For complexes of modules over a commutative ring k, truncated derived Hom takes values in D^{<=0}(k), with derived-tensor composition, units, and the prescribed mapping-space homotopy groups.
notes: Fixed dg-projective replacements; good truncation; Koszul signs; a=k,b=k[1] gives K(k,1).

statement: The general additive relative-category proposal has not been proved from the manuscript’s unspecified additional axioms, or merely from finite-sum closure of a saturated weak class.
notes: Dugger–Shipley’s stronger additive-resolution hypotheses are retained; no general dg-refinement theorem is claimed.

statement: The literal pointed and pointed-ind-category refinements of stabilized full paths remain unresolved in the stated generality.
notes: Exact missing conditions are absorbing zero coherences and compatibility with specified comparisons.

statement: The checked CATHOT all-arrows theorem identifies exact endpoint fibres with path spaces, even translation with identity in Hot, and the one-sided constant-tail maps as weak equivalences.
notes: Supplied proofs independently checked; all-arrows proof cited without being redone; shorter qL proof verified.

statement: The all-type categorical loop model is strictly monoidal, natural in pointed functors, and realizes the loop space with its A-infinity multiplication.
notes: Uses products and concatenation, without pushout-product axioms or fibrant replacement of X.

statement: The all-type endpoint functor is smooth but can fail properness and both strict Grothendieck lifting properties, already for X=[1].
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: VII ms.161-166; Part E; STRATA path test
notes: Empty-type outgoing lift is empty; every proposed incoming terminal path receives two distinct reparametrized maps.

statement: The eventual alternating endpoint functor is smooth and proper but need not be a Grothendieck fibration or opfibration.
notes: Delayed-transition paths in [1] rule out terminal and initial lifts; finite-support truncations cannot settle this.

statement: Every functor has a natural categorical mapping-path factorization into a nerve weak equivalence followed by a smooth proper functor whose strict fibres are homotopy fibres.
notes: Actual functors and base-change argument specified; no claim of a Thomason model factorization.

statement: For the five-element rectangular-band monoid of type S2, the eventual path endpoint map is neither a strict fibration nor opfibration; the all-type map is not an opfibration.
notes: All 125 associativity equations and delayed-transition naturality equations checked; does not refute another bifibration model.

statement: For every n>=1 the specified interval pushout-product is a weak equivalence but not an intrinsic W_infinity-cofibration.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: POLES H.6; TOTASPH F.23; Part E
notes: Explicit sieve pushout changes a contractible source into S3; n=1,2,3 complete tables and rational homology checked.

statement: Finite interval cotensors have a constant-section categorical homotopy equivalence but their exact endpoint fibres need not be the correct path spaces.
notes: X=[1], interval=[1], endpoints (1,0) give empty strict fibre while the topological path space is contractible.

statement: W_infinity smoothness/properness does not imply universal preservation under strict pullback for a larger localizer.
notes: For B C2, rational homology equivalence point→B C2 pulls back to a map with H0 Q^2→Q.

statement: Components of the marked subcategory alone do not specify a stratification whose exit paths compute general localization mapping spaces.
notes: One-object monoid {1,e},e^2=e, with identity marking: contractible classifying space but a two-point endomorphism space.

statement: Existence of another strict bifibration realizing the path local system over the rectangular-band monoid remains unresolved here.
notes: Standard path models fail; their failure is not a proof that no replacement exists.

statement: The checked fixed-origin all-type path category may be contractible without being filtered or totally aspherical; its endpoint functor is final over simply connected bases.
notes: Finite fork and the explicit four-object sphere category give the verified separation.

statement: Finite set-valued restricted Yoneda on finite-category test objects is not faithful: the finitary symmetric-group shift and the identity induce the same tests but are distinct in Hot.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: VIIc-C004 faithfulness question; CATHOT F.2 verification
notes: Actual endofunctor of an infinite one-object category; the proof handles every finite-category test. The equality T^2=1 is independently proved in E.1.
